headline: Core b14g contracts identified from docs and audits; specific deployed addresses not surfaced in accessible sources.

findings.text: Protocol website and documentation fetched successfully; references Core Chain (EVM), Babylon Genesis (CosmWasm), and Bitcoin (native); no block-explorer tag search conducted (Bitcoin has no standard block-explorer name tags for protocols; CORE and Babylon chains not pinned with explorer URLs).

Official docs.b14g.xyz site contains architecture and product pages describing Core Marketplace, dualCORE Vault, and BTCFi Lending Vault, but no canonical 'Deployed contracts' page with address listings was discoverable or fetchable.

Audit links published at https://docs.b14g.xyz/audits list four audits (two by Halborn for Merge Marketplace and dualCORE Vault; two by Halborn and Coinspect for BTCFi Lending Vault and Babylon Merge Marketplace); audit PDF access blocked by permission restrictions.

GitHub org b14glabs identified; multiple repositories listed (b14g-core-subgraph, btc-signature-verify, b14g-btc-dualstaking-tool, yield-server adapters) but no Foundry broadcast or hardhat-deploy artifacts with contract addresses discovered in reachable repos.

Three chains in scope: Bitcoin (non-EVM, no smart contracts), CORE (EVM), Babylon Genesis (CosmWasm). No block-explorer search conducted; Bitcoin lacks standard protocol name-tag infrastructure. CORE and Babylon explorers not probed.
No factory contracts discovered in accessible documentation; cap rule not applicable.

Role taxonomy applied: identified roles include 'marketplace' (Merge Marketplace), 'vault' (dualCORE, BTCFi Lending), 'router' (Re-stake Manager), 'other' (Mapping Contract); actor_class determined as 'unknown' for all (bytecode not queried).
No addresses added to admin_addresses[] because specific deployed contract addresses not surfaced in fetched documentation or accessible audit reports.

rationale.verdict: Discovery incomplete. Three core product components identified from website and docs (Core Marketplace, dualCORE Vault, BTCFi Lending Vault) with audit coverage documented, but specific EVM and CosmWasm contract addresses not accessible via public docs, GitHub deployment artifacts, or audit PDFs (permission-gated). Block-explorer search deferred pending CORE/Babylon chain pinning. Unable to populate admin_addresses[] without concrete addresses.

evidence.shows: Protocol landing page describes b14g as Bitcoin restaking platform enabling BTC holders to earn yield through no-loss restaking.

Audit page lists four security audits: (1) b14g Merge Marketplace (Core) by Halborn, (2) dualCORE Vault by Halborn, (3) BTCFi Lending Vault by Halborn, (4) b14g Merge Marketplace (Babylon) by Coinspect; PDF access behind permission wall.

Detailed architecture of Core Marketplace describing BTC staking orders, CORE staking coordination, and dual-staking reward distribution; confirms contracts deployed on Core Chain but does not list specific addresses.

Main documentation hub describes three product components: BTC Self-Custodial Staking, BTCFi Vaults (dual-staking yield strategies), and Merge Marketplace (on-chain coordination); chains mentioned: Core, Babylon, Stacks.

Babylon governance forum discusses whitelisting b14g's deployer address to enable CosmWasm contract uploads on Babylon Genesis; confirms protocol intends to deploy on Babylon but does not list specific contract addresses.

b14g GitHub organization exists with public repositories including b14g-core-subgraph, btc-signature-verify, b14g-btc-dualstaking-tool; no deployment artifacts (broadcast, hardhat-deploy) immediately visible in search results.

BTCFi Lending Vault documentation describes vault architecture, multi-sig Safe governance, integration with Colend for lending, and CORE token borrowing; confirms smart contract deployment but no specific addresses listed.

Medium article describes Re-stake Manager Contract and Mapping Contract architecture for Babylon BTC staking integration; confirms smart contracts on EVM for Babylon integration but does not provide deployment addresses.

unknowns: D1: CORE chain block-explorer name-tag search not conducted; no CORE or Babylon explorer URLs pinned. Recommend follow-up: site:corescan.com b14g / site:explorer.babylonlabs.io b14g.
D2: No 'Deployed contracts' doc page discovered at /deployments, /addresses, or canonical location; permission-gated audit PDFs may contain addresses.
D3: Audit PDF access blocked; contract addresses likely documented in scope tables. Recommend direct audit PDF download or contact with Halborn/Coinspect.
D4: GitHub deployment artifacts (Foundry broadcast or hardhat-deploy JSON) not discovered in accessible b14g repos. Recommend fork/branch inspection or direct contact.
D5: Bitcoin network has no smart contracts (native staking via timelock); CORE and Babylon explorers not probed.
D8: Cannot populate admin_addresses[] without specific contract addresses. Zero addresses surfaced from accessible sources.

protocol_metadata.about: b14g is a Bitcoin restaking platform enabling no-loss Bitcoin staking across Bitcoin-aligned chains (Core, Babylon, Stacks). Core product components include: (1) Merge Marketplace for coordinating BTC and token staker matching to optimize dual-staking yields; (2) BTCFi Lending Vaults for yield-generating Bitcoin-based asset strategies; (3) BTC Self-Custodial Staking infrastructure allowing native Bitcoin staking with timelock security and no custody risk.
